text_blocks.snippet: Most people with high blood pressure (hypertension) have no symptoms at all, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". You can have high blood pressure for years without realizing it.
Symptoms generally only appear if your blood pressure becomes dangerously high—known as a hypertensive crisis or emergency. These signs may include:

list.snippet: Vision changes (such as blurred or double vision)
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Neurological changes (confusion, weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking)
Nosebleeds or blood spots in the eyes (in some cases)

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: If your blood pressure reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher, wait one minute and test it again.
If it remains that high and you have emergency symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, vision changes, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
If your reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher without symptoms, contact your doctor right away.

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms are rarely present, regular screening is essential. You can learn more about category guidelines from the Mayo Clinic.
If you'd like, let me know:

list.snippet: What recent blood pressure readings you or someone else had
Whether you are experiencing specific symptoms right now
If there is a family history of high blood pressure

text_blocks.snippet: I can help you understand what steps to take next.
